title: 涵光室 Hanguang Shi
subtitle: Changchun Yuan

model.line: A plain box on the block drawn on the Qing plan S01: position and frontage from the plan, heights and roof from the typology of its hall class. It will be updated as the research goes on.

evidence.title: 日下舊聞考 含经堂
evidence.excerpt_zh: 雲容水態西北循山逕入建琉璃坊楔三其北宫門五楹南嚮内爲含經堂七楹後為淳化閣又後爲蘊真齋含經堂東為霞翥樓為淵映齋堂西為梵香樓為涵光室（長春園册）臣等謹案淳化軒内額曰奉三無私聨曰貞石麗延廊畧存古意淳風扇寰宇冀遂初心東西廊廡壁間嵌御定淳化閣帖石刻藴真齋内額曰禮園書圃霞翥樓内額曰味腴書屋
evidence.summary: Three glazed arches, a five-bay gate facing south, the seven-bay 含經堂, then 淳化軒 (printed 閣), 蘊真齋 behind, with 霞翥樓, 淵映齋, 梵香樓 and 涵光室. The rock-cut 淳化閣帖 stones lined the side galleries; 霞翥樓 holds the plaque 味腴書屋.

evidence.title: 涵光室有咏
evidence.locator: v3 p.249, under 含经堂; source ref 7-332
evidence.excerpt_zh: 曰明乃是光，于暗义斯堕。曰暗实无光，试向虚室坐。光固有恒性，明暗无不可。明光灭暗生，暗光灭明作。生灭岂涉光，如是薪传火。
evidence.summary: Poem 涵光室有咏 by the Qianlong Emperor, 1760, filed by the editors under 含经堂.

evidence.title: 涵光室有会
evidence.locator: v3 p.263, under 含经堂; source ref 12-669
evidence.excerpt_zh: 冬室欲其暖，夏室欲其凉。惟有春之室，所喜涵韶光。韶光融户外，十笏中能藏。放弥卷则退，羲经言已详。又如虚生白，颇亦契蒙庄。即景得静会，止止来千祥。
evidence.summary: Poem 涵光室有会 by the Qianlong Emperor, 1775, filed by the editors under 含经堂.

evidence.title: 涵光室口号
evidence.locator: v3 p.265, under 含经堂; source ref 12-962
evidence.excerpt_zh: 涵光室里说涵光，此意分明是注庄。更咏春生何处好，试看止止纳千祥。
evidence.summary: Poem 涵光室口号 by the Qianlong Emperor, 1777, filed by the editors under 含经堂.

evidence.title: 嘉庆帝所题圆明园淳化轩诗考析 (尤李)
evidence.summary: Through Jiaqing's poems. It dates the addition of 淳化轩, 蕴真斋, 三友轩, 静莲斋, 待月楼 and 理心楼 behind 含经堂 to 1770, when the compound reached full size. The 重刻淳化阁帖 stones were set in the galleries in front of 淳化轩.

evidence.title: 圆明园五朝御制诗文集注 v3, editors' note on 含经堂
evidence.summary: The largest group in this garden, finished 1747, rebuilt 1770 with 淳化轩, 蕴真斋, 三友轩, 静莲斋, 待月楼 and 理心楼. 含经堂 is a seven-bay double-eaved glazed hall; 霞翥楼 mirrors 梵香楼 and, with the inner plaque 味腴书室, held the 四库全书荟要, which identifies our 味腴书屋. A stage was added east of 淳化轩 in 1814. Guards were still posted after 1860.

searched: No picture of it found in the Forty Scenes album, its 1745 woodcuts, the Bertin gouaches and the 1887 lithograph; the 20 Xiyang Lou plates; ruin photographs on Commons, at Östasiatiska museet, the Slovene Ethnographic Museum and Historical Photographs of China; today's photographs on Commons.
